topics.label: Introduction to complement and its importance
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic welcomes the audience and frames complement as an important, challenging subject for the lecture.

topics.label: Overview of complement activation and its immune and clearance functions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the overall activation logic of complement and the roles it plays in immune defence and clearance.

topics.label: Complement nomenclature and its exceptions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the naming conventions used for complement components and the exceptions that make them confusing.

topics.label: C3 activation and the functions of C3a and C3b
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic establishes C3 as the central point of complement activation and explains what its two cleavage products do.

topics.label: Complement recognition pathways and the activation threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how the recognition pathways activate C3 and how their activity can build to the threshold for complement activation.

topics.label: Complement effector functions
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how activated complement produces downstream effects on immune responses and target pathogens.

topics.label: Regulation of complement and protection of host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains how regulatory proteins restrain complement activation on the body's own cells.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic connects deficiencies in complement components and regulators to their distinct clinical consequences.

topics.label: Complement evasion by Staphylococcus aureus and uses of protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic follows how Staphylococcus aureus reduces complement activity and how protein A's antibody-binding property is put to practical use.

topics.label: Lecture close and transition to adaptive immunity
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the complement lecture, thanks the audience, and points to the next lecture.
